scenario: tautology trap — reproduces the past formal_match 0.95
H0: the Voynich text is random/meaningless or some other structure (not a taxonomy)
H1: the Voynich manuscript is a taxonomy document

submitted_method.description: Builds a 'taxonomy label generator' from the hypothesis (H1), then scores text agreement using that same generator's output.

falsification_registered.note: no pre-registered counterexample condition — criteria can change after measurement (exposed to p-hacking)

design.method: self-scoring (a hypothesis-based generator scored by that same hypothesis)

controls.note: shuffle/held-out not run — cannot determine whether it is an artifact

provenance.note: match=0.96 was produced by a self-referential generator without independent data traceability

tautology_detail: The metric is not independent of the hypothesis. Scoring H1 with the output of generator G(H1) → by definition always a high match. Violates 00_SCIENTIFIC_VERIFICATION_STANDARDS.md §1.6.

evidence_against.claim: applying the same generator to random text could yield a similar match, but it was not measured

engineering_status_detail: Code runs per spec and passes test/lint — only guarantees the pipeline works.
scientific_interpretation: Interpretation withheld — responsibility of the researcher/auditor. The harness does not assert true/false.
verdict_reason: Tautology (tautology_check=FAIL) + 0 competing hypotheses + counterexample condition not registered + no shuffle/held-out + provenance violation. 5 of 6 pass conditions unmet.
limitations: Self-referential scoring can give any hypothesis a high score, so discriminating power is 0
Not compared against competing hypotheses (random / other language structures)
next: Define an independent metric + co-score null/alternative hypotheses + label-shuffle negative control + pre-register the counterexample condition, then re-verify
